governance.attested_by: run158 endogenous West/Panhandle Waha collapse-frequency (gap G6) 2026-06-25
governance.note: PROBE (not a keeper). run158 = the run154 net-load West/Panhandle Waha delivered-gas-step recipe re-solved with the two-regime SPLIT FREQUENCY made ENDOGENOUS (ercot_west_gas_endogenous_collapse, env ERCOT_WEST_ENDOGENOUS_COLLAPSE=1), closing the last measured input of the West net-load gas shape (forecast-methodology gap G6). Previously the split between the collapsed (deep-negative, low-net-load) and firm (high-net-load) regime was set by the MEASURED Waha negative-price-day frequency (data/raw/ercot_zonal_gas_hub.csv neg_day_freq; 2024 EIA-authoritative 0.42, 2023 0.03, 2025 0.11). It is now derived from FORECAST West/Panhandle oversupply: the fraction of hours West+Panhandle wind+solar generation exceeds local West load plus the region's export takeaway (WESTEX 10.0 GW + PNHNDL 2.68 GW), via fuel.ercot_west_oversupply_collapse_freq, consumed at the run_calibration call site from the same per-zone VRE capacity x CF, load, and transmission topology the model already builds. Every input is a forecast quantity, so the frequency regenerates for any forward year and responds to changed conditions (more West VRE -> more oversupply hours -> higher collapse frequency; unit-tested). The annual-mean Waha basis set by apply_ercot_zonal_gas_basis is still preserved exactly (only redistributed across hours), the deep value still forced by mean-preservation and floored at the physical burner-tip delivered minimum ($0.40), the firm level still the cited firm Waha delivered basis (HH-0.50) — none tuned to a price or volume residual. The measured neg_day_freq is NOT used in this run; it is retained only as the backcast realization, logged alongside the endogenous value on every solve (see the ERCOT West net-load gas step log line) for validation, never re-pinned. Inherited measured levers unchanged from run154: CAMPD unit-level net-load-filtered outage windows, measured ERCOT 60-Day DAM AS series + storage up-AS reservation + load-resource RRS-UFR credit driving the energy+reserve co-opt, measured RTORDPA reliability-deployment overlay, net-load-indexed ST_GAS reliability drag, coal PRB passthrough sigmoid, measured F923/Henry-Hub fuel prices, EIA-860 BTM CHP host steam, Morgan Creek (3492) distillate via oil_primary_bin_fuel, Laredo (3439) West->South zone correction. No unit pinned to its observed CEMS generation; no input rescaled so the model output lands on actuals.
governance.residuals_note: VALIDATION (endogenous vs measured collapse frequency, the central result of this probe): endogenous West-oversupply frequency 0.017 / 0.001 / 0.002 vs measured Waha neg-day 0.030 / 0.420 / 0.110 for 2023 / 2024 / 2025 (in-run, on the dispatched demand+VRE; 2024/2025 clamped up to the 0.01 minimum). The power-oversupply proxy tracks the measured frequency in 2023 (0.017 vs 0.030) but is near-zero in 2024/2025 because West local load plus the 12.68 GW WESTEX+PNHNDL takeaway absorbs essentially all West VRE, so genuine West *power* oversupply almost never occurs. The measured 2024 record (0.42) and 2025 (0.11) were driven by Permian *gas-pipeline takeaway* constraints (associated-gas glut vs constrained interstate capacity), a DIFFERENT physical phenomenon than power oversupply and a measured *outcome* with no forward analogue (CLAUDE.md #12) — so the proxy correctly does not reproduce it. CONSEQUENCE (documented, kept per #1/#11, NOT fit away): with the collapse regime now ~1% of hours instead of the measured 42% in 2024, West gas units see firm Waha (~HH-0.50) in ~99% of hours, so the West CTs (Morgan Creek, Permian, Ector, Topaz) idle rather than running cheap collapse-hour baseload. CT_PEAKER therefore falls below the C1 volume band in all three years: model/EIA-923 5.23/7.56 (2023, -30.8%), 4.95/8.21 (2024, -39.7%), 5.10/7.11 (2025, -28.2%) — vs run154's measured-frequency 5.29/7.20/5.63 (2024 in band). The freed energy lands in CC_REGULAR (142.1/-1.1%, 149.6/+2.9%, 148.5/+4.5%) and COAL_PRB (+3.0/+1.7/+2.0%), which stay near band. This makes the run158 BACKCAST FIT WORSE than run154 and is exactly why it is registered as a PROBE, not promoted: removing the measured collapse frequency reveals that run154's in-band 2024 West-CT dispatch was partly carried by a measured gas-takeaway outcome that has no forward analogue. The structurally-correct endogenous mechanism is KEPT (the forward model must respond to VRE build, which a frozen measured 0.42 cannot); the West-CT under-run is the open root cause for future work (the West/Permian CTs serve large local load and are not transmission-closable, per the run154 Far_West-split rejection), and is never closed by reverting to the measured frequency. Price/shape limitations inherited from the energy-only dual (run151/run154) are unchanged.
